title: Harvest and Smile
premise: Cyrus Crane, a reclusive urban explorer, discovers a network of tunnels beneath his inherited family house that appear on no survey and seem to breathe with the rhythm of the building above. As every mirror in the house begins reflecting the rooms one second late, Cyrus realizes the delay is not an echo but an invitation—something below has learned to imitate him, and it is wearing his reflection to walk among the living. Digging into his grandmother's journals, he learns the family duty he fled: each generation must feed the thing beneath or it will wear their faces until nothing of them remains. In the final hours before sunrise, Cyrus chooses love over inheritance, burning the mirrors and sealing himself in the tunnels with the entity so his partner, Ada, can live unhaunted—ending with her, years later, finding one mirror that reflects a room where someone is still counting doors.
about_author: Dominic Eastwick is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping municipal infrastructure before turning to fiction about the spaces maps refuse to record. He writes in basements and claims he has never once trusted a reflection.

chapters.title: The Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Establishes his ritualized, invisible life: locking doors, logging tunnels, keeping Ada at arm's length without telling her why. He maps a tunnel that shouldn't exist beneath the house's foundation. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline, and the first crack in his control.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The bathroom mirror reflects him raising a hand a beat after he does. He tests every reflective surface; all lag by exactly one second. Ada visits and notices nothing, which terrifies him more. Emotional beat: creeping dread and the isolation of seeing what others cannot.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept Below
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, intercut with grandmother Edith's journal entries from 1962. He finds her hidden study behind a mirrored wardrobe, learning the family fed 'the Tenant' below for generations. Emotional beat: the sickening discovery that his invisibility was inherited, not chosen.

chapters.title: The Second Cyrus
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. His reflection stops mimicking and starts acting independently—smiling when he doesn't, mouthing words. Neighbors greet him warmly for conversations he never had. Emotional beat: horror of identity theft from inside his own skin, and paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Ada, Uninvited
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She arrives unannounced and meets 'Cyrus,' who is warm, open, everything she's wanted—and subtly wrong. She finds his logbook with tonight's date already filled in, describing her arrival. Emotional beat: love colliding with the realization that the man she loves may already be replaced.

chapters.title: The Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Trapped in the house as night falls, he reads Edith's final pages: the Tenant honors invitations, and Edith invited it in to save Cyrus as a child. The debt has come due. Emotional beat: rage and grief—his whole constrained life was a mother's bargain gone wrong.

chapters.title: Doors Opening Downward
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Every door in the house opens onto tunnel mouths. The false Cyrus hunts Ada through shifting corridors while the real one navigates Edith's tunnels toward the chamber below. Emotional beat: desperate flight, the two Cyruses converging on the same heart of the house.

chapters.title: The Tenant's Face
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the chamber he confronts the Tenant wearing his face perfectly, offering a trade: stay below willingly and Ada goes free, refuse and it takes them both. It shows him memories only he possesses. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible arithmetic—duty fulfilled means self erased.

chapters.title: Sunrise Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Climax. Cyrus's POV. As dawn nears, he accepts—but on his terms: he shatters the great mirror, breaking the Tenant's anchor, and drags it down with him as the tunnels collapse. Ada escapes into morning light. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed from duty into choice, love as the final act.

chapters.title: Counting Again
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, years later. She has kept the house, sealed the tunnels, lived. One evening she finds a small mirror in the wall cavity reflecting a room one second late—and in it, faintly, someone counting doors, patient, smiling. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; love outlasts death, but inheritance never quite ends.
